subject: Re: Order form — invoicing split, tax liability, and PO routing
messages:

Cc: DataWorks Procurement <procurement@dataworks.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — invoice split + tax responsibility question

Hi Mina,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. A couple of quick items procurement asked me to confirm before we circulate internally:

- Do you support splitting invoices across a US HQ entity and a Canadian subsidiary? We often get billed to two entities and need separate invoice lines for services originating in each country.
- For Canadian deals, we need clarity on who is responsible for GST/HST — customer or vendor? Your standard OF wording is ambiguous to our tax team.
- Our procurement prefers Net45 payment terms; your order form currently shows Net30. Is Net45 acceptable for this engagement?
- We will raise a PO when terms are agreed — do you require a specific PO structure or contact to send it to?

Attached is our PO template for reference. If easier, can we schedule a 15-min call to lock this down?

Thanks,
Sofia Martins
Head of Vendor Ops | DataWorks Inc
sofia@dataworks.com

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form — invoice split + tax responsibility question

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in finance (Marissa) and legal (Karthik) to confirm operational / contractual items. Quick answers up front:

- Invoice split across entities: we can support split invoicing but need the billing entity names and tax IDs on the PO.
- Tax responsibility: by default our OF places taxes as "customer responsibility"; legal may propose more explicit language for Canada.
- Net terms: we typically do Net30, but we can be flexible for strategic accounts. I'll confirm with Marissa on Net45 feasibility.
- PO routing: send POs to invoicing@redwoodinference.com and cc accounts-receivable@redwoodinference.com; we can accept a PDF PO or a procurement system export.

Please find a refreshed draft Order Form attached (order_form_v3.pdf) with a proposed invoicing schedule (section 2.3) that supports split invoices. Karthik — would appreciate a quick pass for the Canadian tax language. Marissa — can you confirm whether finance is OK with net45 for this deal and whether we should invoice from the US or set up a Canadian billing entity?

If a short call helps, I can send a 15-min invite for later today or tomorrow.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order form — invoice split + tax responsibility question

Mina / Sofia — quick legal notes after a first pass on order_form_v3: see attached redline (order_form_v3_redline.docx). High level:

- Tax clause: Recommend replacing the generic clause with: "All taxes, duties, and similar governmental charges (excluding taxes on Redwood's income) arising from the transactions, including any Canadian GST/HST, shall be the responsibility of Customer unless Customer provides valid tax documentation demonstrating exemption. If Customer is required to self-assess under the reverse charge mechanism, Customer will notify Redwood in writing prior to the first invoice."
- Invoice split: We can permit split invoices but need invoice-level billing entity, billing address, and tax ID for each line. Add the requirement to Exhibit B (billing details).
- Payment terms: We can accommodate Net45 on a per-deal basis; propose a contract-level checkbox in the OF to capture agreed net terms and any early-pay discount. Note that extended terms may affect credit review timing; finance will advise.
- PO acceptance: Add a short clause that a PO does not modify the OF unless signed by an authorized Redwood signatory.

Sofia — if you can confirm whether DataWorks requires Redwood to register for GST/HST in Canada (unlikely for our typical delivery model), we can advise whether an invoice from US entity is sufficient or we need a Canadian billing entity.

Attaching the redline.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: order_form_v3_redline.docx (45KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Martins <sofia@dataworks.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form — invoice split + tax responsibility question

Thanks — tagging in finance detail:

- Net45: We can approve Net45 for DW-2027-0042 provided the deal credit review completes and the PO is submitted before we schedule the first invoice. Please expect a 2–3 business day onboarding window after PO receipt for billing setup.
- Billing entity: We prefer to bill from our US entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.) unless DataWorks specifically requires a Canadian invoice. If DataWorks requires Canadian invoicing, we will need to issue invoices from our Canadian subsidiary; that requires tax registration and will delay the first invoice by ~10 business days.
- Taxes: Per legal, taxes are customer responsibility. If DataWorks is subject to reverse charge, include their tax reference on the PO and notify us so we don't remit GST/HST.
- PO routing: Send POs and any credit docs to invoicing@redwoodinference.com and include accounting@dataworks.com in the body for faster processing.

Accounting contact for remittance and PO questions: accounts-payable@redwoodinference.com

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
